title: Getting Started with spawnBayes: A Clemens Creek Sockeye Example
text: spawnBayes estimates salmon spawner abundance run timing repeated live-count surveys. Unlike traditional area---curve approaches, spawnBayes estimates abundance, run timing, associated uncertainty allowing residence time vary among years. underlying methodology described Thompson et al. (2026). Additional features introduced Thompson et al. (2026) include support survey-error groups, allowing separate observation-dispersion parameters estimated different survey types quality classes, optional robust observation model reduces influence anomalous survey counts. vignette demonstrates complete analysis using sockeye salmon survey data Clemens Creek, BC, Canada. data provided Diana McHugh, South Coast Stock Assessment, Fisheries Oceans Canada.

title: Getting Started with spawnBayes: A Clemens Creek Sockeye Example
text: diagnostics() function summarizes several indicators MCMC sampling performance model convergence. example, diagnostic checks acceptable. divergent transitions detected, maximum tree-depth warnings encountered, largest Rhat value close 1. Effective sample sizes bulk tail regions posterior distribution sufficient reliable inference. fitting new datasets, users pay particular attention : Divergences: zero whenever possible. Tree depth hits: frequent hits may indicate model settings adjusted. Rhat: values close 1 indicate convergence, values substantially greater 1 suggest poor mixing among chains. Effective sample size (ESS): larger values indicate better estimation posterior summaries. recommendation column provides summary whether additional model tuning longer runs required.
code: diagnostics(fit) #>   converged    quality divergences treedepth_hits max_rhat min_ess_bulk #> 1      TRUE acceptable           0              0    1.008          331 #>   min_ess_tail      recommendation #> 1          636 No action required.
